name: HCDS - Health Care Delivery Solutions (MHS GENESIS Follow-On)
vendor: TBD — Pre-solicitation phase. Leidos holds $1.4B+ sole-source bridge through ~2028.
description: The competitive follow-on to DHMSM — the $5.5B program that delivered MHS GENESIS to 3,200+ locations serving 9.5M beneficiaries. DHA released a draft MOSA contract strategy Dec 22, 2025 splitting the program into separate vehicles: (1) PMO/Systems Integration, (2) Product/Software Support (likely Oracle direct), and (3) Service/OCM/Analytics. Industry feedback closed Jan 9, 2026. Government review ongoing — Feb 6 update noted 'a lot of great feedback' requiring extended review (promised update by Feb 20 but no confirmed public post since). RFI close date: Aug 30, 2026. No draft RFP yet. The Hegseth PAE restructuring (Nov 2025) moves HCDS under a Phase 2 Software and Business Systems Portfolio — signing authority still in transition. Leidos's Oct 2025 $570M enterprise services task demonstrates the bridge is actively funded while HCDS planning proceeds.
sb_note: Vehicle 3 (Service/OCM/Analytics) likely to include small business set-aside carve-outs based on DHA pattern

name: MHS GENESIS (DHMSM Bridge)
vendor: Leidos / Oracle Health (Cerner) / Accenture Federal Services / Henry Schein
description: DoD enterprise EHR deployed at 3,200+ locations serving 9.5M beneficiaries and 205,000 providers. Deployment completed 2024. The sole-source bridge was justified by two factors: (1) documentation gaps — MHS GENESIS documentation lived inside Leidos's institutional knowledge, preventing competitive transition, and (2) the February 2024 Change Healthcare ransomware attack forced DHA to reassess documentation security. Oct 2025: $570M enterprise services task. The MOSA-based HCDS follow-on is designed to break this single-SI dependency by making capabilities modular and independently competable.

name: PEO DHMS CSO (Competitive Solutions Opening)
description: DHA's non-traditional acquisition pathway under OTA authority (10 U.S.C. § 4022). Active AOIs: 1b (AI/ML/NLP, proposals due July 1, 2026), 4 (Data Applications — canceled due to McKinsey task order dispute, but requirement remains valid). AOI 3 (Ambient Listening/DAX Copilot) established a critical precedent: successful CSO prototypes can transition directly to production task orders under the DHMSM/HCDS IDIQ without a new competitive recompete. This 'CSO-to-IDIQ' pathway is being closely watched as a model for closing the valley of death between prototype and production. Innovation threshold (DFARS 212.7001) is a binary gate — must demonstrate a 'new application' of technology, not merely commercial technology at its intended use.
sb_note: Open to small businesses and non-traditional contractors under OTA

name: Enterprise Intelligence & Data Solutions (EIDS)
vendor: SpinSys-Diné ($35M PMO support, 8(a) tribal); Koniag Government Services (AWS cloud, 8(a))
value: Multiple vehicles (PMO: $35M; AWS cloud and analytics: values vary)
description: DHA's enterprise data and analytics program — not a single contract but a PMO administering multiple vehicles. Key accomplishment: Operation Helios migrated 1 petabyte of data (MDR + M2 legacy warehouses) into the MHS Information Platform (MIP) on AWS GovCloud — the largest data migration in DHA's 10-year history. MIP now serves 20,000+ users across 100+ MTFs. SpinSys-Diné (Navajo Nation / Diné Development Corporation) holds $35M PMO support under 8(a) sole-source (awarded Sept 2024). Koniag Government Services provides AWS GovCloud infrastructure under 8(a). Key leader: Chris Nichols, who led Operation Helios and favors open, API-led architectures over proprietary platforms. AOI 4 (Data Applications) was canceled but the underlying AI-on-MIP requirement remains active.
sb_note: 8(a) tribal sole-source lanes for PMO and cloud infrastructure; analytics lanes may be competed

name: DHA Enterprise Generative AI
description: First Impact Level 5 generative AI platform authorized for Protected Health Information in the Military Health System. Awarded Dec 2025. Ask Sage's IL5 ATO for GenAI covering PHI is extraordinarily difficult to obtain — establishing significant first-mover advantage in DHA enterprise AI. Separately, DHA has restricted Anthropic (Claude) models in classified/sensitive environments, making AWS Nova the preferred LLM option for future MHS AI deployments. The March 24, 2026 White House National AI Policy Framework — preempting state AI laws and creating a unified federal AI standard — provides a tailwind for IL5 AI adoption across the MHS.
sb_note: Ask Sage is a small business

name: VA EHRM (Electronic Health Record Modernization)
description: VA's enterprise EHR modernization replacing VistA. Only 6 of 164 VA medical centers live as of March 2026 — 158 remain on legacy VistA. April 2026: 4 Michigan sites go live (Detroit, Saginaw, Ann Arbor, Battle Creek), followed by 9 more in Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky, and Alaska. Performance record is the primary driver of Congressional pressure: VA IG documented 826 major performance incidents since first go-live, GAO found only 13% of staff believe the system makes VA more efficient, and 58% believe it increased patient safety risks. FY2026: $3.4B allocated but 30% ($1.02B) withheld until July 1, 2026 pending VA conditions. Oracle exercised 3rd option period in 2025. Rep. Budzinski's 33-page discussion draft (March 2026) proposes a 2-year clock: if VA can't certify improvement and complete 2 new deployments, Oracle contract extensions would be restricted. Oracle facing reported 20-30% layoffs that could further strain EHRM staffing.

name: Federal Electronic Health Record Modernization (FEHRM)
vendor: Oracle Health (Cerner) — same platform for both agencies
description: Joint DoD-VA office coordinating EHR interoperability. Both agencies use the Oracle Health platform, but government ownership, data governance, and workflows differ. DoD completed MHS GENESIS deployment (2024). VA has 6 live sites with 13 planned for 2026 and ~145 remaining — estimated completion no earlier than 2031. FEHRM must maintain interoperability across 4 environments: DoD MTFs on MHS GENESIS, VA sites on new Oracle EHRM, VA sites still on legacy VistA, and community care providers under CCN. Interoperability requirements mandate FHIR R4, HL7, and the TEFCA/RCE framework. CMS is also moving to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for Medicare — creating a 3-agency Oracle ecosystem (DoD + VA + CMS) with significant platform convergence.

name: Community Care Network Next Gen (CCN NG)
description: Next-generation VA community care IDIQ replacing current CCN regional contracts (Regions 1-6). Solicitation 36C10G26R0003 on SAM.gov. Multiple-Award IDIQ for national/regional health plans governing how veterans receive care at community providers. Contains a binary past performance gate: multi-state coverage documentation. This is pass/fail — cannot be overcome with other evidence. Operationally connected to Bi-Directional Imaging (36C10B26Q0076), which enables imaging data from community providers to return to VA. A firm holding both CCN NG and Bi-Directional positions has end-to-end community care coverage.

name: T4NG2 (VA IT Services)
agency: Department of Veterans Affairs / VA TAC
vendor: 30+ awardees (21 SDVOSBs including GovCIO, Cognosante MVH, Booz Allen Hamilton, SAIC, Leidos)
description: VA's primary enterprise IT services vehicle — successor to T4NG ($22.3B, ~64% obligated). Awarded Oct 2023 to 30+ primes including 21 SDVOSBs. Task orders began March 2026 after one of the most contentious protest sagas in federal IT: 31 companies filed protests, only 3 prevailed (Taurian, Technatomy, Peregrin added via corrective action). Historical dominance: Booz Allen captured ~$4B+ of T4NG (via Liberty IT acquisition); GovCIO captured ~$1B. GAO ruling established that SDVOSB eligibility must be maintained through award date, not just proposal date. Covers full IT spectrum: systems engineering, cybersecurity, AI/ML, healthcare IT, EHRM support. Multi-agency access available beyond VA.
sb_note: 21 of 30+ awardees are SDVOSBs or SDVOSB JVs

name: VA Health Connect / IHT 2.0
vendor: 9 IDIQ holders: Agile4Vets, Arrow ARC, Blue Water Thinking, Greenside Solutions, Prometheus Federal Services, Reefpoint Group, Rios Partners, Titan-Auxo, Tribility
description: VA's 24/7 virtual care, clinical triage, and tele-emergency program for veterans. IHT 2.0 is the underlying 100% SDVOSB set-aside IDIQ, awarded late 2025. VA Health Connect functions include nurse triage hotline, telehealth coordination, clinical triage and escalation, and tele-emergency for veterans unable to reach VA facilities. Key competitive dynamic: Arrow ARC (JV with Aptive Resources) captured 91% of all IHT 1.0 spending — the dominant incumbent. Task orders compete among the 9 IDIQ holders. OIP (Office of Information and Provider Programs) task order is in active procurement, with draft RFP in hand and final RFP expected April 7-14, 2026.
sb_note: 100% SDVOSB set-aside IDIQ — all work flows through veteran-owned firms

name: VA Enterprise Imaging (NEIS + Multi-VISN PACS + Bi-Directional)
description: Three connected VA imaging modernization procurements: (1) NEIS — National Enterprise Imaging Solution (36C10X25Q0015, est. $300-500M, FY2027) replacing fragmented PACS/VNA across 170+ VA medical centers. (2) Multi-VISN PACS (36C10X24Q0024, est. $50-90M, Q3 2026) modernizing imaging across multiple Veterans Integrated Service Networks. (3) Bi-Directional Imaging (36C10B26Q0076, est. $15-30M, Q2 2026 — most imminent) enabling imaging data from community care providers to return to VA. Currently, VA often receives only a bill from community radiologists — not the imaging data. Bi-Directional connects directly to CCN Next Gen's community care infrastructure.
sb_note: SDVOSB prime paths available through JV vehicles

name: JOMIS / OMEIS (Operational Medicine Systems)
vendor: Leidos (JOMIS, under MHS GENESIS prime); OMEIS vendor TBD
value: Part of MHS GENESIS program; OMEIS est. $10-50M
description: Two related operational medicine IT systems: JOMIS (Joint Operational Medicine Information Systems) is the deployed/theater version of MHS GENESIS for disconnected, low-bandwidth military operations — installed on USNS Mercy, integrated with MedCOP for real-time force health tracking. OMEIS (Operational Medicine Enterprise Information System) replaces the legacy Defense Teleradiology System (DTRS/Medweb) for operational tele-radiology. Sources Sought (HT003824R0005) closed June 2024; no RFP released yet. COs: Elizabeth Ruckwardt and Jena Bowman at DHMS-CD, Rosslyn. AFS holds adjacent $24M JOMIS contract (HT003823C0004).
sb_note: OMEIS likely to be competed; set-aside TBD

name: PEO DHMS Deployment Solutions (New IDIQ)
vendor: TBD — draft RFP feedback due March 11, 2026
description: Solicitation HT003826RE001 — new Multiple-Award IDIQ for on-demand deployment of health IT solutions. Scope: site preparation, training, user adoption, and post-installation support for MHS GENESIS and OpMed product deployments. Evaluation includes two challenge scenarios (Federal EHR deployment and OpMed product deployment). Small business participation goal: 30% total. CO: Joyce Elaine Pace-Reed (DHMS-CD). Draft RFP feedback due March 11, 2026 — formal solicitation expected to follow.
sb_note: 30% small business participation goal with sub-goals for SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone, SDB

name: DHA Telehealth Programs
vendor: Amwell + Leidos (Digital First, $180M); MHS Global Nurse Advice Line: bridge HT001124C0011 ($24.6M)
description: Two key DHA telehealth programs: (1) Amwell Converge platform ($180M task order with Leidos) replacing MHS Video Connect as the enterprise virtual health platform — supports synchronous video, async messaging, care coordination, and MHS GENESIS workflow integration. (2) MHS Global Nurse Advice Line (HT001124C0011, $24.6M bridge contract) providing 24/7 nurse triage globally. The bridge indicates an upcoming recompete — similar in function to VA Health Connect's IHT 2.0. The Nurse Advice Line recompete could be set-aside for small business if DHA follows recent patterns.
sb_note: Various task orders; Nurse Advice Line recompete may be small business eligible

name: IHS Health IT Modernization (RPMS Replacement)
description: Enterprise EHR replacing RPMS (Resource and Patient Management System) — IHS's legacy EHR built in-house since the 1980s, serving 2.6M American Indians and Alaska Natives across 575+ federally recognized tribes and 170+ facilities. GDIT awarded Nov 2023. Platform: Oracle Cerner (same base as DoD MHS GENESIS but different configuration). Key IHS-specific factors: tribal sovereignty means facilities may opt in or out; Buy Indian Act creates set-asides for Indian-owned businesses; many facilities in remote, low-connectivity environments requiring offline capability. GDIT team approach: human-centered design, tribal consultation and data sovereignty compliance, Oracle Federal FedRAMP High hosting, IHS EPLC alignment.
sb_note: Buy Indian Act set-asides for tribal-owned firms; OCM and analytics sub-positions available under GDIT

name: CMS Rural Health Transformation
description: CMS $50B program strengthening rural healthcare infrastructure across all 50 states, awarded Dec 2025. Scope explicitly includes AI workflow modernization alongside telehealth, cybersecurity, and provider network development. The rural focus means telehealth-integrated AI tools for small/rural provider networks — a domain where adoption friction is highest. Task orders under the 50-state IDIQ structure could range $5-20M per state/region for AI workflow modernization specifically. Matthew Versaggi (White House Presidential Innovation Fellow at CMS) is directly adjacent to the policy governing this initiative.
sb_note: State-level awards include small business set-aside structures

name: HHS HOPSS - HHS One Professional Services Solutions
agency: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
description: A $3.6B small business vehicle covering HHS-wide STEM and IT services — health data analytics, cybersecurity, and digital transformation for CMS, CDC, NIH, and FDA. If awarded, HOPSS provides direct vehicle access for HHS-wide work without needing to sub through a prime. Draft RFP expected April-May 2026. Award expected April 2027. This vehicle could structurally resolve CMS entry challenges for small businesses currently limited to subcontractor paths through GDIT or Peraton portfolios.
sb_note: Small business set-aside — $3.6B vehicle for HHS STEM/IT services

name: HHS Cybersecurity and Data Management FY2026
agency: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
description: HHS cybersecurity work flows through established vehicles (CDM DEFEND is Booz Allen at $1.2B). Watch for task orders on CIO-SP3 or OASIS+ with small business set-asides. Multiple solicitations expected across FY2026 covering zero trust, continuous monitoring, and health data protection for CMS, CDC, NIH, and FDA systems.
sb_note: Task orders on CIO-SP3 or OASIS+ may include small business set-asides

name: CMS Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)
description: CMS migrating mission-critical Medicare claims processing to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure on FedRAMP High. Announced Feb 2026. Combined with DoD MHS GENESIS (Oracle Health) and VA EHRM (Oracle Health), this creates a 3-agency Oracle ecosystem. Oracle's simultaneous investment in cloud datacenters for AI/LLM workloads may be diverting resources from federal health services — Oracle facing reported 20-30% layoffs with Oracle Health expected to take cuts to fund datacenter investments.

name: TRICARE Managed Care Support - T-5 (MCS)
description: Managed healthcare delivery for 9.6M+ TRICARE beneficiaries. T-5 generation went live Jan 1, 2025, replacing T-2017 contracts. Dec 2025: DHA exercised Option Period Two — $7.34B for Humana, $719.4M for Evernorth pharmacy. This is managed healthcare contracting, not IT — but the budget scale ($8B+ annual) sets context for understanding DHA's overall health spending priorities.

name: TEFCA / RCE (Health Information Exchange)
description: Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement — foundational nationwide health information exchange mandated by 21st Century Cures Act. Sequoia Project operates as Recognized Coordinating Entity (RCE), enabling interoperability across DoD, VA, CMS, and all federal health systems. FEHRM interoperability requirements mandate FHIR R4, HL7, and TEFCA/RCE compliance for all MHS and VA solutions.

name: CDM DEFEND (Health Data Cybersecurity)
description: Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation DEFEND program. Protects health data and IT infrastructure across all HHS agencies including CMS, CDC, NIH, FDA. Implements zero trust architecture and continuous monitoring. Booz Allen also holds significant DHA analytics positions and is a credible competitor for HCDS Vehicle 3 analytics lanes.

name: MPSM (Medicare Payment Systems Modernization)
description: Legacy Medicare claims system transformation. GDIT holds MPSM contracts; CMS CG&PM recompete is also a GDIT path. Multiple task orders for modernizing Part A, B, and D payment processing. Small businesses can access CMS analytics work through GDIT sub paths or through the upcoming HOPSS vehicle.

name: TPharm5 (TRICARE Pharmacy)
description: TRICARE pharmacy benefit management. Express Scripts manages Rx benefits, claims, mail-order pharmacy, and retail network for all TRICARE beneficiaries. CY2026 option exercise: $719.4M.

name: DHA Zero Trust 2.0 / GSP
description: FY2026 initiative consolidating expiring health IT infrastructure contracts under a Global Service Provider model with Zero Trust 2.0 architecture. Covers network ops, endpoint security, cloud infrastructure for the MHS. Part of the broader PAE restructuring under Hegseth's Nov 2025 Warfighting Acquisition System memorandum.

name: DHA Data Governance (WOSB Set-Aside)
description: Solicitation HT001126RE011 — WOSB set-aside for enterprise data governance using a VAULTIS-Guided Framework. Scope: comprehensive baseline data inventory, centralized metadata repository, Analysis of Alternatives for enterprise data catalog, and automated metadata harvesting tools. Performance period Jan 30, 2026 to Jan 29, 2027 with 12-month options. Connects to the EIDS/MIP data fabric infrastructure. CO: contact via SAM.gov listing.

name: CDC DCIPHER (Disease Surveillance)
agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
description: Palantir Foundry for disease surveillance, outbreak detection, and population health monitoring. Originally COVID-19, expanded to broader surveillance. Palantir also attempted DHA health IT entry through CSO framework but encountered government preference against proprietary platform approaches.

name: SSA DCPS2 (Disability Claims Processing)
description: Disability claims processing modernization with heavy health records integration. Processes medical evidence for disability determinations.

name: NIH STRIDES (Cloud for Biomedical Data)
description: Discounted commercial cloud access for NIH-funded biomedical research, genomics processing, and AI/ML workloads.

name: CDC DIBBs (Data Integration Building Blocks)
agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
description: Modular data integration platform for state/local/tribal public health agencies. Standardizes disease reporting and lab results. Deploying to 30% of STLTs by 2026.
